Public speaking practice, minus the homework energy

Icebreakers was built by people who loved what speaking clubs could do — and got tired of what they cost and how stiff they felt. So we made our own. It's run entirely by its members, and it will cost you exactly nothing, forever.

$0

The price of admission

No membership dues, no per-meeting fees, no upsell at the door. Free isn't a promotion here — it's the whole point.

The other guys vs. us

The traditional route

Annual dues, manuals, titles, parliamentary procedure, and a vibe that can feel like a dentist's waiting room with speeches.

The Icebreakers way

Show up, grab a seat on the rug, speak when you're ready. Feedback is kind, direct, and actually useful — and somebody will make you laugh before the night's over.

Real skills, real reps

Prepared speeches, impromptu speaking, debates, and evaluations — the reps that build actual confidence for work presentations, job interviews, toasts, classrooms, and every other moment a room full of eyes lands on you.

Led by members, not bosses

The club was formed as a free alternative — then handed to the members to run, because a speaking club should be led by the people doing the speaking. The young leaders here run the show.

What a meeting actually looks like

Ninety minutes, a printed agenda waiting on the table when you walk in (yes, we really print one — times, names, roles, down to the minute), and we're wrapped by 8:30 so your evening is still yours. The flow goes something like this:

7:00 PM

Warm-up & word of the day

We settle in and somebody introduces a gloriously nerdy word of the day — like cryophilic: "thriving in cold environments." Very on brand.

Next

Prepared speeches

Members deliver speeches from our own 20-project manual — from your very first Icebreaker talk all the way up to advanced storytelling and debate.

Halfway

Table Topics

Two minutes, zero preparation, one ridiculous prompt. The most fun you can have with your heart pounding. (Try it below!)

Then

Friendly feedback

Every speaker gets an evaluation that's honest without being harsh — what landed, what to try next time, and plenty of what to keep doing.

By 8:30

Debate-night energy

Some nights end in a full debate — argued hard, laughed about harder. Recent rulings below. The rematch arguments continue in everyone's heads all week.

Try a Table Topic right now

This is the exact muscle we train: get a prompt, talk for a minute or two, survive, thrive. Draw one and try it out loud — nobody's timing you. Yet.

Your prompt

Hit the button and take the mic…

At a real meeting you'd get 1–2 minutes, a room that wants you to win, and applause either way. Online, you get this button and our complete faith in you.

Warm-up round: unlimited retries, zero judgment.

The debate-night hall of fame

Serious skill-building, deeply unserious subject matter. These highlights are distilled from the club's Facebook page — the memes themselves live there, posting fresh every week. Rulings are final, grudges are forever.

Settled debate

Optimus Prime vs. Godzilla

Mentor vs. mentee, maneuvering vs. muscle. The room argued it like it mattered — because for one night, it absolutely did.

Verdict: FLIGHT beat FIGHT
Word of the day

Cryophilic

(adjective) — thriving in cold environments, uniquely adapted to low temperatures. Leadership without a little cryophilic spirit gets soft pretty quickly.

Status: adopted as a lifestyle
The eternal question

Best speaker, or best arguer?

Polished speakers lose to sharper arguments. Razor-sharp arguments die when nobody can follow them. At Icebreakers, the judges still have to pick one.

Verdict: still fighting about it

Fresh debates, meeting photos, and the meme stream live on our Facebook page — follow along and argue with us.

Monday nights, in pictures

Real meetings, real members, one very good rug. Tap any photo for a closer look.

Come sit in — guests are the whole point

No sign-up, no RSVP, no pressure to speak on your first night (or your fifth). Just show up upstairs and grab a chair.

Why Icebreakers exists

Lafayette Icebreakers was formed as a free alternative — the fun, no-dues speaking club people wished existed, with the gavel handed straight to the members. Twenty-eight members strong and counting, it's theirs now.
